rule.name: SwiftUI ATS Relaxation Enabled
rule.rule_desc: The checked source contains a transport-security exception, insecure endpoint, or certificate-validation configuration. Resolve the effective policy and the connections it governs.
rule.vuln_desc: An attacker on the network may read or alter affected traffic if sensitive data travels over cleartext or the connection accepts an untrusted server. Normal HTTPS endpoints and correctly implemented validation do not establish exposure.
rule.developer: Use HTTPS with normal certificate-chain and hostname verification. Remove permissive production callbacks and broad transport exceptions; restrict any justified exception to a documented, non-sensitive endpoint.
rule.reviewer: Review transport security keys in Info. plist. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: SwiftUI Insecure URL Usage
rule.rule_desc: The code declares an entry point, model, destination, or configuration value that may cross a trust boundary. Identify callers, recipients, and the required data-access policy.
rule.vuln_desc: A boundary that trusts unauthorized callers or exposes private output may permit data disclosure or state changes. A declaration, address, or architectural marker alone does not establish such a failure.
rule.developer: Trace the actual boundary, restrict accepted inputs and recipients, and enforce authentication and object-level authorization where required. Verify both authorized and denied use cases.
rule.reviewer: Audit endpoint strings and networking clients. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: SwiftUI Dynamic Web Content Injection Marker
rule.rule_desc: The application exposes script execution or a native interface to rendered web content. Resolve the content source and effective origin restrictions.
rule.vuln_desc: Attacker-controlled content may execute in a trusted page or invoke native operations, exposing application data or privileges when origin isolation and operation authorization are insufficient.
rule.developer: Restrict loaded origins, avoid interpolating untrusted data into scripts, and expose only required native operations with input validation and per-operation authorization.
rule.reviewer: Review web view wrappers and script execution boundaries. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.vuln_desc: An attacker on the network may read or alter affected traffic if sensitive data travels over cleartext or the connection accepts an untrusted server. Normal HTTPS endpoints and correctly implemented validation do not establish exposure.
rule.developer: Use HTTPS with normal certificate-chain and hostname verification. Remove permissive production callbacks and broad transport exceptions; restrict any justified exception to a documented, non-sensitive endpoint.
rule.reviewer: Inspect networking trust challenge handlers. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: SwiftUI Sensitive Data in UserDefaults Marker
rule.rule_desc: The application stores sensitive values or configures protection for persistent data. Determine the actual storage location, backup policy, and lock-state access restrictions.
rule.vuln_desc: An actor with access to unprotected application files, backups, or overly broad keychain access may recover credentials or private records and use them outside the intended trust boundary.
rule.developer: Use the platform credential or key store for secrets and appropriate authenticated encryption and file protection for private records. Minimize stored data, backup exposure, and lock-state accessibility.
rule.reviewer: Review storage APIs for token/credential keys. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: SwiftUI Pasteboard Sensitive Data Marker
rule.rule_desc: The application reads the shared clipboard or pasteboard. Review whether the read follows an explicit paste action and whether the returned content enters logs, storage, or network requests.
rule.vuln_desc: Passwords, payment details, or other private content copied from another application could be collected or disclosed if clipboard reads occur without user intent or the content is sent to an unauthorized recipient. Platform access restrictions and the actual handling of the data determine exposure.
rule.developer: Read clipboard content only for an explicit user paste action. Process only the value needed for that action, avoid logging or transmitting it unnecessarily, and respect platform clipboard access restrictions.
rule.reviewer: Audit clipboard operations and data classification. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: SwiftUI Hardcoded Secret Marker
rule.rule_desc: The checked source or build configuration embeds potentially sensitive credential or key material. Determine whether it is active and whether it reaches distributed artifacts or logs.
rule.vuln_desc: A party who can read exposed source, artifacts, configuration, or logs may recover active secrets and access the protected service or decrypt data with the secret owner’s privileges.
rule.developer: Remove active secrets from source and build layers, rotate exposed values, and load replacements through a restricted secret-management facility. Use narrowly privileged, short-lived credentials.
rule.reviewer: Validate no production secrets are committed. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.
